caption: HW2: Mesh Atlas — from a 3D viewer to a learning application
text: Mesh Atlas extends the homework one viewer with neural network predictions. It classifies synthetic meshes as ellipsoids, cuboids, cylinders, or tori. The original rotation, wireframe, upload, and annotation tools are still available.

caption: A real request: mesh triangles → geometry features → trained MLP → probabilities
text: Clicking Predict shape sends triangle coordinates to a local Fast API service. The trained model identifies this torus and returns probabilities for all four families. It never receives the filename or the example label.

caption: Independent examples: new geometry produces new predictions
text: Here are two different meshes. Selecting an ellipsoid and then a cylinder produces fresh predictions from their geometry. These example objects were generated independently of the training, validation, and test sets.

caption: Upload a binary STL mesh and classify it directly in the viewer
text: The same pipeline works with uploaded files. This binary STL contains a cuboid. It is parsed by the browser and classified by the backend, without opening a notebook or manually running an inference script.

caption: 24 inputs → 48 ReLU units → 48 ReLU units → 4 outputs; 3,748 parameters
text: The model is a small multilayer perceptron with two hidden ReLU layers. Twenty four geometric descriptors summarize an area sampled surface. This keeps the network understandable and fast on a CPU, while allowing nonlinear combinations of shape features. Training uses cross entropy and mini batch gradient descent.

caption: Held-out test: MLP 595/600 correct (99.17%); shallow baseline 591/600 (98.50%)
text: The curves show measured training and validation loss and accuracy. On six hundred held out objects, the reference network makes five errors, versus nine for logistic regression using identical features. The confusion matrix shows most errors involve cylinders and cuboids. Checkpoint selection uses validation loss; test data never supply training gradients.

caption: Bonus: change hyperparameters and follow real training/validation updates
text: The interactive training challenge is implemented here. I can change the learning rate, epochs, hidden width, layer count, and activation. Starting a run initializes fresh weights. These curves update from actual backend measurements. Test metrics appear only after training has finished and the validation checkpoint has been selected.

caption: Activate the newly trained checkpoint and predict through the same interface
text: After the run completes, this button activates its trained weights. Returning to the viewer uses the new model for prediction. The original reference model stays available and can be restored, so experiments do not overwrite the submitted checkpoint.

caption: Synthetic benchmark only • trained weights, code, data and AI disclosure included
text: These results are limited to four procedural shape families. Real scans, incomplete surfaces, and unknown objects are not validated, and softmax scores are not calibrated confidence. The repository includes source code, trained weights, reproducible data, tests, references, and an AI assistance disclosure. Both interactive training and the training monitor are demonstrated.
